interest: Japanese intelligence in wartime Turkey and Allied pressure.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.20267) documents Japanese military intelligence, espionage, and diplomatic activities in Turkey during 1944. The records reflect mounting Allied concern over Axis collaboration and the threat posed by Japanese intelligence networks operating out of neutral Turkey, which compromised American diplomatic security in Ankara and threatened Allied communications and supply routes to the Far East. The file comprises an internal State Department memorandum from January 1944 on safeguarding the U.S. Embassy in Ankara, an Office of Strategic Services (OSS) cross-reference sheet regarding German-Japanese collaboration, and British diplomatic telegrams from November 1944 detailing coordinated Anglo-American plans to urge the Turkish government to break diplomatic ties with Japan and dismantle Japanese intelligence missions.
